summary: Susumu Yamaguchi was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Otani University, Paris, and Kyoto, under Lévi, Sasaki, Teramoto, and de La Vallée Poussin. He served as professor at Otani University (1934–1964).

Suwanda H. J. Sugunasiri is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Nalanda College, London, Pennsylvania, and Toronto. He founded and served as president of the Nalanda College of Buddhist Studies, and held posts at Toronto and Ontario Tech University.

Suzanne Karpelès was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Lévi, Foucher, and Finot. She held posts at the EFEO, the National Library of Cambodia, and the Buddhist Institute.

Suzanne Newcombe is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned her doctorate at Cambridge. She has held posts at the LSE, Cambridge, Inform, King's College London, and the Open University as senior lecturer in Religious Studies.

Sven Hedin was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and history scholar. He studied at Stockholm University (~1886–1888), Uppsala University (1888), the Humboldt University of Berlin (~1889–1890), and the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1892).
Sven Sellmer is a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and computational studies. He has held academic posts at Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf and Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań.
Sven Wittemann is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned his Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Kapila Abhayawansa (attested 2014).
Swami Lakshman Joo worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, studying under Maheshwar Nath Razdan from 1926 to 1933. He later founded the Universal Shaiva Fellowship in 1991.

Swami Maheshanandagiri Maharaj is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who served as Mahamandaleshvar Pontiff at Dakshinamurti Peetha (attested 1980). He founded the Mahesh Research Institute and Advaita Grantha Ratna Manjusha.
Swami Satyananda Puri was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Calcutta and later held an academic post there.
Swami Siddheswarananda was a scholar in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Madras and held a post with the Ramakrishna Order from circa 1920 to 1957.
Swami Vimalananda was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Ripon College. He was a disciple of Swami Vivekananda in 1897.
Swami Vishnudevananda was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied as a disciple under Sivananda Saraswati (~1947–1963). He founded the International Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres.

Swami Vivekananda was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Presidency University, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta, and was a disciple of Ramakrishna from circa 1881 to 1886.
Sydney Frank Markham was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at Wadham College (~1919–1923). He served as Secretary and then President of the Museums Association (~1929–1942).

Syed Ali Bilgrami was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Patna College, Lucknow, IIT Roorkee, the Royal School of Mines, and London. He served the Government of Hyderabad (~1879–1901) and was Reader in Marathi at Cambridge (1901).

Syed Ameer Ali was a history, archaeology, and religious studies scholar. He was educated at Aliah University and the University of Calcutta (~1863–1868), where he later held a post from circa 1877 to 1887.

Syed Hasan Askari was a historian and Indologist who studied at Zila School Chapra, Langat Singh College, and Patna University. He served as Director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute from 1968 to 1971.
Syed Nawab Ali was a scholar of history and archaeology. In 1932, he is attested as Principal of Bahauddin College and Professor of Persian at the Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda.
Sylvain Brocquet is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure (1980) under Marie-Claude Porcher, and held a post at Aix-Marseille University.
